title: Petits Pois à la Française
subtitle: Peas braised with baby onions, lettuce, and butter
excerpt: Fresh or frozen peas braised slowly with baby onions, lettuce, bacon lardons, and butter until everything is tender and the liquid has reduced to a sweet, silky glaze. The classic French way with peas.
sourceNotes: Petits pois à la française is one of the signature preparations of the classical French kitchen. Auguste Escoffier, Le Guide Culinaire (1903), establishes the method as the standard treatment for fresh garden peas. Julia Child, Mastering the Art of French Cooking (1961), gives the home version. The combination of lettuce (usually the outer leaves of cos/romaine), baby onions, and butter appears consistently across all sources. The lettuce wilts into the braising liquid and adds a delicate sweetness.

content.text: Petits pois à la française is the opposite of boiled peas: instead of cooking quickly in boiling water, the peas braise slowly with butter, baby onions, and shredded lettuce. The lettuce adds sweetness as it melts into the liquid, and the final dish is much more complex in flavour than plain peas. Frozen peas work very well here, making this a year-round recipe despite its spring associations.

items.prepNote: divided: 30 g at start, 20 g to finish

content.text: Melt 30 g of the butter in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the lardons (if using) and cook for 3 minutes. Add the pearl onions and cook for 5 minutes until beginning to colour.

Add the peas, shredded lettuce, sugar, stock, and a pinch of salt. Stir to combine. Cover and cook over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the peas are tender and the lettuce has wilted completely. Stir occasionally.

Remove the lid and increase the heat. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until most of the liquid has evaporated and the peas are glazed. Add the remaining 20 g of butter and swirl to combine. Taste and season. Scatter with parsley and serve.

items.symptom: The peas are grey and overcooked
items.cause: The braise was cooked at too high a heat, or for too long.
items.fix: Keep the heat very low once the lid goes on. Peas are cooked in 12 to 15 minutes; any more and they will become mealy and grey. Frozen peas need less time than fresh.

items.cause: Too much stock was added, or the lid was removed too late.
items.fix: Remove the lid and increase the heat for 3 to 4 minutes to evaporate the excess liquid. The final dish should be glazed, not soupy.

content.text: Petits pois à la française is a dish of the Paris vegetable garden tradition. The finest early peas came from Clamart and Saint-Germain-en-Laye, the market gardens that supplied Les Halles. The technique of braising peas with lettuce and butter, rather than simply boiling them, is a specific French approach. The method appears in French cookery writing from the 17th century onwards and has remained largely unchanged. The dish is at its best with very fresh or very young frozen peas; older peas need more sugar and longer cooking to work.
